questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text: During bronchoscopy, a physician notes that the right main bronchus appears almost a direct continuation of the trachea. Why is this clinically significant?

options.option_text: It allows equal ventilation of both lungs
It increases airflow resistance to the right lung
It predisposes to aspiration of foreign bodies into the right bronchial tree
options.explanation:
The right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left.
Its alignment with the trachea forms the most direct path for inhaled material, making it the common site for aspiration and obstructive pneumonia in the right lung.

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: The femur is classified as which type of bone?
questions.hint: Other options: Short bones (carpal, tarsal), flat bones  scapula, cranial), irregular bones (vertebra).

options.option_text: A. Short
Long
options.explanation:
Long bones have two ends and a shaft. Examples include the femur, clavicle, and humerus.

 

Other options: Short bones (carpal, tarsal), flat bones (scapula, cranial), irregular bones (vertebra).

questions.hint: Which of the following bones is an example of a

options.option_text: Clavicle

options.explanation:

Other options: Clavicle is long; humerus and radius are also long bones.

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

options.option_text:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text: During bronchoscopy, a physician notes that the right main bronchus appears almost a direct continuation of the trachea. Why is this clinically significant?

options.option_text: It allows equal ventilation of both lungs
It increases airflow resistance to the right lung
It predisposes to aspiration of foreign bodies into the right bronchial tree
options.explanation:
The right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left.
Its alignment with the trachea forms the most direct path for inhaled material, making it the common site for aspiration and obstructive pneumonia in the right lung.

options.option_text: It indicates congenital malrotation of the trachea

questions.question_text: A penetrating wound at the fifth intercostal space on the mid-clavicular line injures the pleural covering of the lung. Which layer is directly torn before reaching the lung tissue?

options.explanation:
The visceral pleura directly covers the lung surface.

A deep stab that passes through the parietal pleura and pleural cavity reaches this layer before entering lung tissue.
Breach of visceral pleura causes pneumothorax with collapse of the corresponding lung due to loss of negative intrapleural pressure.

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: The femur is classified as which type of bone?
questions.hint: Other options: Short bones (carpal, tarsal), flat bones  scapula, cranial), irregular bones (vertebra).

options.option_text: A. Short
Long
options.explanation:
Long bones have two ends and a shaft. Examples include the femur, clavicle, and humerus.

 

Other options: Short bones (carpal, tarsal), flat bones (scapula, cranial), irregular bones (vertebra).

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:

Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

options.explanation:

Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

options.option_text:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text: During bronchoscopy, a physician notes that the right main bronchus appears almost a direct continuation of the trachea. Why is this clinically significant?

options.option_text: It allows equal ventilation of both lungs
It increases airflow resistance to the right lung
It predisposes to aspiration of foreign bodies into the right bronchial tree
options.explanation:
The right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left.
Its alignment with the trachea forms the most direct path for inhaled material, making it the common site for aspiration and obstructive pneumonia in the right lung.

options.option_text: It indicates congenital malrotation of the trachea

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text: A patient develops obstruction of the nasolacrimal duct. Tears overflow onto the face because the normal drainage pathway into which the duct opens is blocked. Which specific site of drainage is affected?

options.option_text: . Inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha
options.explanation:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

options.option_text:
The nasolacrimal duct opens into the inferior meatus of the nasal cavity.
Obstruction prevents tears from draining, leading to epiphora (tear overflow).
The relation of the duct to the conchae is a key applied point for ENT and lacrimal surgery.

questions.question_text: Following surgery for chronic sinusitis, a patient complains of reduced sense of smell but intact nasal breathing. Which area was most likely affected during the procedure?

options.option_text: Roof of nasal cavity and superior concha
options.explanation:
The olfactory mucosa occupies the roof, upper nasal septum, and upper surface of the superior concha.
Damage here affects olfactory nerve endings, producing anosmia, though the lower respiratory part of the cavity still functions normally for airflow.

questions.question_text: During bronchoscopy, a physician notes that the right main bronchus appears almost a direct continuation of the trachea. Why is this clinically significant?

options.option_text: It allows equal ventilation of both lungs
It increases airflow resistance to the right lung
It predisposes to aspiration of foreign bodies into the right bronchial tree
options.explanation:
The right main bronchus is shorter, wider, and more vertical than the left.
Its alignment with the trachea forms the most direct path for inhaled material, making it the common site for aspiration and obstructive pneumonia in the right lung.

options.option_text: It indicates congenital malrotation of the trachea

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme

questions.question_text:
A 22-year-old medical student presents with fatigue and muscle weakness after prolonged exercise. Laboratory tests show elevated levels of muscle glycogen and no rise in blood lactate after exercise.
Which enzyme is most likely deficient in this patient?
questions.hint: Think about an enzyme that breaks down glycogen in skeletal muscle to release glucose during anaerobic exercise. If this enzyme is missing → muscle cannot get energy → cramps + no lactate increase.

options.option_text:
A. Glucose-6-phosphatase
B. Debranching enzyme
C. Muscle phosphorylase
D. Acid maltase (α-1,4-glucosidase)
E. Branching enzyme
options.explanation: Debranching enzyme
